protein kinase C (PKC) is a Ca(2+)/phospholipids-dependent enzyme, which is involved in the proliferation of transformed liver cells.
protein kinase C is a Ca2+/phosphoinositide-regulated protein kinase that is involved in signal transduction in the regulation of cell growth.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of protein kinase C in the control of growth and differentiation of normal, preneoplasia and neoplastic cells.
the role of the protein kinase C in the regulation of growth and transformation of rat liver cells.
the relationship between protein kinase C activity and the proliferative capacity of T51B rat hepatocytes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
protein kinase C is not involved in the Ca2+-dependent control of growth of T51B liver cells.
the protein kinase C activity in T51B rat-liver cells is not directly involved in the regulation of cell proliferation.

protein kinase C is involved in the regulation of the growth of normal rat liver cells and that this enzyme may be involved in the regulation or expression of the neoplastic phenotype of T51B rat hepatoma cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the loss of Ca2+-dependency of growth of T51B rat hepatoma cells was associated with a loss of Ca2+/phosphatidylserine-dependent protein kinase activity.

the loss of Ca2+-dependent cell growth regulation in transformed T51B rat hepatocytes correlates to an altered Ca2+-dependent protein kinase C activity, and this change may be related to an altered Ca++/phospholipase C activity.
the ability of transformed cells to proliferate under Ca2+-deficiency conditions correlates to a high level of protein kinase C activity in the cell.
The main takeaway from our work is that
protein kinase C activity is a useful marker for the neoplastic transformation of T51B cells.
the ability of transformed cells to grow in Ca2+-free medium is a consequence of the increased levels of Ca2+/phosphatidylserine-dependent protein kinase activity.
Ca2+ plays an important role in the regulation of cell proliferation and that protein kinase C activity is a marker of transformed cell growth.
